messages:
ivy: hitting inconsistent yields from client.stream_tool_call in async mode — sometimes yields raw str frames, sometimes parsed dicts; breaks downstream pydantic parsing.

ivy: tiny repro:
```
async for pkt in client.stream_tool_call(model="gptx-tool", tool="extract_struct", input=prompt):
    print(type(pkt))
```

ivy: seen: '"{\"id\":1, \"data\":' then next yield '{"id":1, ...}'

raj: sounds like transport frame splitting. we currently json.loads per frame — should buffer until complete object.

lucy: agreed. proposal: default behavior should yield only fully parsed objects; add opt-in raw_frames=True to expose low-level strings. also add stream_tool_call[T] typed variant that runs T.parse_raw for pydantic models.

raj: also be careful around reconnects/retries — ensure buffer state is reset only when server indicates object boundary, not on transient reconnects. add unit tests that split JSON at random byte offsets.

ivy: rel note: will open GH issue with logs + sample + CI link.

ci-bot: https://ci.redwood/9999/streaming-toolcall-flake (flaky test)

lucy: action items: (1) implement incremental buffer & tests (high), (2) add raw_frames debug flag (low), (3) design stream_tool_call[T] + docs (medium).

ivy: thanks folks — temporary workaround is to use non-streaming call_tool or user-side buffer.
